edits_applied.before: After the victories, opinion abroad shifted. The empire had been at peace so long that its armaments had gone slack, and the overseas powers, talking of wealth and strength among themselves, still whispered that China was frail even after it had put down one great crisis after another. Once Zuo had dealt with Pasha, the foreigners began to tell the story about. On his first arrival in the capital, a church tower in the Inner City overlooked the palace, and popular rumor said the Marquis Zuo would have it torn down; he posted a proclamation to explain, and the talk stopped.
